problem: The text says velocities agree at rc but surface slopes do not. With K = ω rc², the free-surface slope dz/dr = vθ²/(gr) is also continuous at rc; only the curvature changes. A student will expect a kink that is not there.
fix: Change to: 'Velocities and surface slopes agree at rc, though the curvature changes; this is the matching condition for the Rankine model.'

problem: The text says a forced vortex needs torque to overcome friction between neighbouring rings, and Q4 says neighbouring rings slide over each other with vorticity 2ω. In steady rigid-body rotation vθ = ωr, adjacent rings have the same angular speed; the strain rate is zero, so there is no inter-ring shear/friction. Vorticity 2ω is element spin, not sliding between rings.
fix: Rewrite: in a real cup the impeller supplies torque to overcome wall friction and to maintain the rotation against losses; adjacent rings do not slide relative to each other in steady rigid-body rotation, so inter-ring friction is not the reason.

problem: The answer compares the surface dip/rise and explains why the free vortex has the larger dip, but it does not answer the part about energy stored.
fix: Add an explicit energy sentence: at r = 0.8 m the free vortex has the larger local speed (3.75 m/s vs 2.4 m/s), so it stores more kinetic energy there; in the ideal free vortex the energy near the axis diverges, which is why a real finite core is needed.
